after visiting some of the newer gym locations such as coleraine and ballymena i can see that there are a number of improvements that could be made to the lisburn gym to offer the members better facilities especially in the functional area and weight training areas. the list of suggestions is as follows: 1. install a track and sled, with the correct plates to load the sled made available in this area. 2. install a rack of blk box hex dumbbells in the functional area to offer dumbbell weights from 5kg to 22.5kg as is the case with the newer gyms. the current options only go as far as 10kg which is too light for a number of exercises that would be performed in this area. additionally the hex shape is much more suited for functional exercises than the circular ended dumbbells that lisburn currently has. 3. renovate the weight training area to install a blk box rig with weightlifting platforms like there is in the newer gyms. this would increase the number of people who can train at any one time. i acknowledge there is limited space in the venue but i believe that with some reorganisation this could be accommodated given that e.g. coleraine has all of the suggestions on my list and is working with a much smaller venue. 4. this is linked to point 3 - i suggest adding additional 15kg barbells and replacing/servicing the older barbells that lisburn currently have. in the newer gyms ive observed that there are usually 3 15kg belfast bars, and a good number of 20kg belfast bars and power bars, easily catering for everyone at the gym, whereas lisburn is quite limited in comparison. additionally there are not enough 5kg olympic lifting plates (only 1 pair) which is problematic if someone takes these away from the weight lifting platform. i suggest buying at least 1 new pair of these for the current situation, however if there was to be a rig installed plates would have to be bought in proportion to this. 5. add 2 concept bikes, to the functional area. ive noticed that lisburn only has the concept ski erg and rowers, however it would be a welcome addition to be able to have access to concept bikes here too. 6. the flooring in the functional area is spongey making it less stable that the flooring ive experienced elsewhere, and the area itself is quite small. i suggest that the area is refloored with the same material as in the newer gyms and the equipment rearranged to enable this area to cover a larger surface area. thanks for taking the time to read my review, and i hope that in time all of the suggestions can be accommodated given this is the standard of equipment and facilities already being offered in the newer gyms.

half-price subscription, for the highest tier, becuase it wasnt that expensive, and wanted to see how things went. i ended up going once so my initial idea was to change my subscription to the lowest tier and keep trying. the website does not help you with this, and actively confuses. there is no way to downgrade via the website. the "instructions page" i was directed to provided instructions that werent possible, and there was nothing else to try. it is intentionally designed to be difficult, and needs to be improved. i then froze my subscription (before the renewal date), not wanting to cancel but wanting time to think and not spending any more money. i thought because i froze it before the renewal, i wouldnt pay. i was wrong. i got charged another Â£24.99, and felt cheated out of my money (of which i dont have much). i am now aware that you have to freeze probably 5 days before the renewal, or cancel your direct debit and thus cancel your sub, to not be charged. the service needs to be improved, especially as there are many people (including me) who struggle with phone calls/face-to-face interaction. it is not justifiable to profit by intentionally making your service less accessible. it is a heavily gendered space with little privacy in the changing room (mens, for me). there is no gender-neutral changing space. if you arent comfortable changing/showering in public, i have been a member of a puregym in central london. one of the attractive features of puregyms in london are the classes. however, if your fitness regime is class-based (spin, circuits, aerobics etc) as opposed to just using the gym for the machines, then puregym is a problem. unlike other gyms where members can book and attend as many classes as they wish, puregym places a limit on the number of classes that its members can book over a seven day period. puregym is not as pure as it claims to be. members can only book a maximum of 8 classes over a seven day period. this has caused endless problems and frustration for puregym members who have not been listened to by the companys membership and marketing department. it seems to be all about the money! for puregym. about a months ago, puregym introduced a new membership category called puregym extra - for an extra Â£5 per month, standard rate members can get an upgrade which allows them to (1) book classes up to 14 days in advance; (2) access other puregyms that are within the same (or lower) member subscription rate as their home gym; (3) pause their membership for free for 3 months; and (4) bring a friend to workout for free up to 4 times each month.on the face of it, puregym extra seems like a good deal. but it isnt and heres why:- even though members who pay extra can book their classes 14 days in advance, their allocation of 8 classes stays the same! instead of allocating extra members 8 classes for every 7 days (which would mean a total of 16 classes over 14 days), puregym extra members have actually had the number of classes they can book reduced!- access to other puregyms within the same or lower member rate as your home gym was something which puregym standard rate members already had! what puregym did was to sneakily withdraw this entitlement from standard fee-paying members and re-package this as an extra. why are we paying Â£5 more for a service/ benefit that we already had?!- bringing a friend to workout for free up to 4 times per month may seem like a benefit worth paying for until you realise that all you are doing is acting as a marketing executive for puregym! puregym give away hundreds of free gym passes via groupon, wowcher and other discount/ incentive routes all the time in the hope of converting one-off visitors into monthly fee-paying members. they have been offering deals and prizes to members who refer-a-friend for ages, so this latest ploy is nothing new.- again, pausing your puregym membership for three months for free seems like an extra benefit, but when you think about it, is it really free? standard rate members have to pay Â£5.99 for each month they pause their membership. when you realise how little extra you are actually receiving for your additional Â£5 per month as a puregym extra member, you realise that the Â£15 that you are purportedly saving on pause has already been paid to puregym by you 20 times over! how many of us actually pause our gym memberships anyway? those of us who unwittingly upgraded our membership to puregym extra, did not realise that there was really no benefit until after we upgraded - puregym conveniently failed to publish the small print about the maximum 8-class rule applying over 14 days as opposed to 7 days. they failed to notify us that access to other puregyms within the same home gym member rate had been removed from standard membership. so. there it is! you can see that the trump capitalists up at puregym hq sat around the table one day and hatched a plan to get their puregym members to pay more for something that they already had, whilst at the same time getting less! confused?! you should be, because that is how many puregym members feel at the moment. confused and conned!we do have the option of quitting our membership of puregym in protest. that still remains an option. in the meantime, we choose to publish our concerns in the hope that puregym will see sense and rectify the chaos that it has created for its members, trainers and instructors.we think that this is one for trading standards!
